name: Ditch Damsel
imitates: A damselfly nymph tied hook-point up with a two-tone wire body and marabou wing, so it swims slim, wiggly and snag-resistant in lakes, ponds and slow water.
recipe: Two olive wires and one silver wire, wrapped together

steps.text: Lay a smooth thread base, then wrap Mirage tinsel forward over it to the hook eye and tie it off.
Catch two olive wires and one silver wire behind the eye and wrap them back together in tight turns to the bend, leaving a short tinsel tag. Twist the wire ends off flush.
Invert the hook and lash melted mono eyes about an eye length behind the hook eye with X wraps.
Tie in a squared marabou feather behind the eyes so it extends a shank length past the bend.
Add four to six mottled mallard fibers behind the eyes, a few on each side of the wing, and trim the butts.
Tear a sparse clump of olive rabbit fur from the hide, about half the wing length, and bind it on top behind the eyes. Trim the butts.
Loop Sili Legs around the shank in front of the eyes and lay them along the sides. Dub a thin thread.
Color the eyes with a black marker, then fold the wing, rabbit and legs forward over the eye and prop them up with dubbing behind.
Dub forward in X wraps through the eyes into a round head, whip finish and trim the legs to the end of the wire body.
